messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
అతడు ఆమెను ప్రతి పట్టణంలో వేటాడుతాడు, అతను ఆమెను నరకంలోకి తిరిగి పెట్టేవరకు, అక్కడ ఇర్ష్య మొదట ఆమెను పంపింది.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Questi | Agent (male) who will hunt | అతడు | he | OK | | la | Patient (female) of the hunt | ఆమెను | her (ACC) | OK | | caccerà | Future verb “shall hunt” | వేటాడుతాడు | will hunt | OK | | per | Preposition “through” (traversal) | (part of) **పట్టణంలో** | in/through the town | OK | | ogne | Quantifier “every” | ప్రతి | every | OK | | villa | Noun “town” (location) | **పట్టణంలో** | in the town | OK | | fin | Subordinator “until” (temporal limit) | (part of) **పెట్టేవరకు** | until | OK | | che | Complementizer “that” (introduces clause) | — (implicit) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | l’avrà | Auxiliary “shall have” (future perfect) | — (implicit) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | rimessa | Verb “set back” | పెట్టే | set | OK | | ne | Preposition “in” (locative) | (part of) **నరకంలోకి** | into | OK | | lo | Definite article “the” (masc.) | — (none) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | ’nferno | Noun “hell” (destination) | **నరకంలోకి** | into hell | OK | | là | Adverb of place “there” | అక్కడ | there | OK | | onde | Relative adverb “whence” (causal) | — (implicit) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | ’nvidia | Noun “envy” (personified cause) | ఇర్ష్య | envy | OK | | prima | Temporal adverb “first” | మొదట | first | OK | | dipartilla | Future verb “shall send forth” | పంపింది | sent | OK |
---
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: `che`, `l’avrà`, `lo`, `onde` – these function words or articles are not required in Telugu and are therefore omitted. - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none.
All source lexical items are represented in the Telugu translation, and the grammatical agreements (gender, number, tense) are appropriate for the target language.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
